Subject: Boundary validation: control plane / data plane egress and TLS termination

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the architecture docs you shared last week. We're doing a final validation for our Private VPC deployment and need to confirm a few things before we lock the firewall rules and ASN peering:

- Control plane reachability: do you require outbound connectivity from our control-plane-facing subnets to 3 specific Redwood endpoints, or is there a single regional FQDN we should allow?
- TLS termination: we want TLS termination at our edge — are customer edge TLS terminators supported (we terminate at our edge) or do you require mutual TLS to Redwood's ingress? Any details about client cert rotation would help.
- Egress ports: which source/destination ports & protocols are required for the data plane (inference traffic) vs control plane (model management, metrics)?
- BGP / ASN mapping: if we do a direct BGP session for failover, what's the expected ASN ranges and prefixes you advertise?

Can you send a single-page boundary diagram we can share with our networking team and a short port matrix? We may have to present this to our security/compliance committee on Friday.

Appreciate your help — copying Grace (network engineering) who will own the firewall changes.

Thanks,
Elliot Shaw
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Granite Biotech

Attachment: granite-requirements-v1.pdf (requirements summary)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Boundary validation: control plane / data plane egress and TLS termination

Elliot — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then attachments and next steps below.

- Control plane: outbound from your control-plane subnets to regional FQDNs are sufficient — we publish three regional endpoints per cloud provider (see diagram). We prefer DNS allowlist rather than IP ranges since we may rotate IPs for scaling.
- TLS termination: We support both modes. For regulated customers we recommend mutual TLS (mTLS) terminated at the Redwood edge; we can also support end-to-end TLS where you terminate at origin and our connections use mutually authenticated connections for control signals. If you pick customer-edge termination, we require that Redwood's control plane uses mTLS for control signals and that inference traffic uses TLS1.3.
- Ports: attached is a port matrix with control vs data plane ports (eg. 443, 7443 for control; 50051/443 for gRPC/HTTP inference; 123/UDP if you opt into NTP sync). See egress-port-matrix-20280723.csv.
- BGP / ASN: For direct peering we accept private ASNs; we advertise a /24 per region by default. For handoff details see the annotated diagram.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-boundary-draft-20280723.pdf (diagram), egress-port-matrix-20280723.csv (port list)

Next steps:
- Naomi will confirm the exact FQDNs and mTLS cert rotation cadence
- Kimberly can walk the Granite networking team through the BGP snippet if you want to try a test session next week

I'm free Thursday 14:00-16:00 PT for a 30‑minute call. Would that work?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Boundary validation: control plane / data plane egress and TLS termination

Elliot — adding a few technical specifics below that your firewall team will want:

- Control plane FQDNs (example): cp-us-west-1.redwood-inference.com, cp-us-east-1.redwood-inference.com
- IP rotation model: endpoints resolve to a short-lived set of IPs (rotated via DNS). Recommend DNS allowlist with a 300s TTL check during rollout.
- Ports (high level):
  • Control plane: TCP 443 (mTLS), TCP 7443 (webhooks), TCP 5222 (optional agent tunnel)
  • Data plane: TCP 443 (HTTP/gRPC), TCP 50051 (gRPC alt), UDP 53 (dns) only for resolver
  • Health/monitoring: outbound 8125/UDP for statsd push (optional)
- mTLS certs: Redwood rotates client certs quarterly; we can accept your CA bundle and issue short-lived client certs for control plane access. We'll provide a cert rotation playbook and automated ACME-based option if you'd prefer.

I've attached a small CSV with the port matrix and an annotated PNG showing where TLS is terminated in each mode.

If you want to test a sample connection, we can open a temporary diagnostic session and share tcpdump snippets from our side.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
